# THEME LIBRARY — the factory theme catalog

> **Version:** 1.2 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active
> **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK, TOKEN_FILE, THEMING_MANUAL, DESIGNER_PLAYBOOK

> **Scope:** first family — **Metro Warm** (Cyber Pharma: Mist / Slate / Bright / Dark-deep). Further theme families append here as new projects derive them; the pattern is app-agnostic.
> **Reader:** Designer (me, in future labs) + Claudy.
> **Pairs with:** the **Global Design System Handbook** (defines the token *contract*) and each project's **token file** (`globals.css` — the live values). This doc is the *catalog*: named themes that each satisfy the contract.
> **Mental model:** the Handbook says *which tokens must exist*; `globals.css` holds *the active values*; this library is the *menu* of complete value-sets you can drop in. Adding a theme never touches the contract — only values.
>
> **v1.1 reconciliation note (2026-06-08):** Two changes only. (1) The live token file is **`globals.css`**, not `TOKEN_FILE.md` — references corrected throughout (the Global Design System Handbook §8 names `globals.css` as the primary deliverable; this aligns to it). (2) Role identity tokens (`--role-*`): the RULES were written here (§2). *(v1.2 note: they are now **defined in the contract** — GDSH §2 — with **reference values minted in TOKEN_FILE**; the reconciliation this note started is complete on both sides, F-043.)*

---

## 1. How a theme entry works

A theme = **one complete semantic token set** (every token the Handbook requires), in HSL-no-wrapper, activated by a class on `<html>`. Components never change; only the variables behind `bg-primary`, `bg-card`, etc. resolve differently. That's the whole "change values, not code" promise.

- **Light-base themes** live on `:root` (or a `.theme-*` override).
- **Dark-base themes** live on `.dark` (or `.dark.theme-*`).
- Full values for the two defaults are in `globals.css` (`:root` + `.dark`); the alternates are the small `.theme-*` override blocks there.

---

## 2. The "Metro Warm" family (Cyber Pharma v1)

Shared across **all four** (these never change between modes — brand + meaning + identity hold):

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary (brand) | coral `#f9704f` → `12 93% 64%` |
| Success (recovered) | green — `131 54% 40%` light / `142 69% 58%` dark |
| Destructive (money lost) | red — `2 67% 51%` light / `351 95% 71%` dark |
| Info (neutral count) | blue `#2f7ce0` → `214 74% 53%` |
| Warning (pending) | amber `#e8a008` → `41 93% 47%` |
| Role — superadmin | identity hue, distinct from brand & status *(set per family; AA on `--card`)* |
| Role — admin | identity hue — **must not reuse the destructive red** |
| Role — member | identity hue — may align with `--success` |
| Typeface | Saira |
| Radius | `0` (Metro flat) |
| Labels | uppercase, tracked |

> **Role tokens (added v1.1):** roles are identities, not statuses. They hold their hue across all four modes just like the semantic four. The only hard rule: `--role-admin` must read as visually distinct from `--destructive` so an admin badge never looks like an error. Tune each role's lightness per mode and contrast-check on the style tile.

What changes between modes is **only the neutral surface stack**:

### 🟫 Mist — *default light*
- **Base:** light · **Background:** `#e2e5ea` (`217 16% 90%`) · **Surface:** `#ffffff`
- **Activate:** `:root` (default — no class)
- **Best for:** the everyday daytime view. Muted, easy on the eyes, looks intentional rather than glaring. **This is the recommended default.**

### 🌑 Slate — *default dark*
- **Base:** dark · **Background:** `#1d212a` (`222 18% 14%`) · **Surface (card):** `#2e3440` (`220 16% 22%`)
- **Activate:** `class="dark"`
- **Best for:** low-light work, long sessions. Sophisticated gunmetal; coral pops hardest here.
- **Readability note (L16):** background sits *below* the card so panels elevate; `--muted-foreground` is lifted (`221 17% 71%`) and `--border` firmed (`218 13% 33%`). This is the v1.1 real-screen fix — keep it; do not flatten background and card to the same value.

### ⬜ Bright — *alternate light*
- **Base:** light · **Background:** `#ffffff` · **Surface:** `#ffffff`
- **Activate:** `class="theme-bright"`
- **Best for:** maximum contrast, print/export views, screenshots for decks. Crisp but can glare on big screens.

### ⬛ Dark-deep — *alternate dark*
- **Base:** dark · **Background:** `#191c24` (`224 18% 12%`) · **Surface:** `#23262f`
- **Activate:** `class="dark theme-deep"`
- **Best for:** OLED / focus mode / demo drama. Near-black; reserve for when you want the charts to glow.

**Phase 1 ships Mist + Slate** wired to the theme toggle. Bright and Dark-deep are catalogued and ready, not yet wired.

---

## 3. Adding a new theme (the repeatable process)

1. **Pick the neutral direction** — only the surface stack changes (background, card, muted, border, secondary). Brand + semantic + role stay fixed.
2. **Derive the full set** — every token the Handbook lists, light *and*/or dark base. Don't ship a partial theme.
3. **Contrast-check** — run `success`/`destructive` (and the `--role-*` colors) as small text against the new `card`; tune lightness until all clear WCAG AA. (This is the step a 4-color palette can't give you.)
4. **Add as a class** — a `.theme-*` override block in `globals.css`. Nothing else changes.
5. **Catalog it here** — name, base, background, "best for", activation class.
6. **Render the style tile in it** — eyeball light + dark, then a real-screen pass, before locking.

A new theme is ~30 minutes and zero component changes. That's the payoff.

---

## 4. Per-tenant brand themes (multi-tenant, future)

Cyber Pharma is multi-tenant. When a client wants their own brand color, it's the same mechanism scoped to a class:

```css
.theme-acme { --primary: <acme hsl>; --ring: <acme hsl>; --accent: <acme hsl>; }
```

- Swap **only** `--primary` / `--accent` / `--ring`. **Never** the semantic four or the role tokens — underpaid must read red, and an admin must read like an admin, for every client.
- Apply the class at the tenant boundary (layout reads the org's theme).
- This keeps a per-pharmacy brand a one-line addition, not a fork.

> Defer building this until multi-tenant brand theming is actually scoped (it's Phase 7-ish). The architecture above means it costs nothing to add later.

---

## 5. Quick reference — activation

| Theme | Class on `<html>` |
|---|---|
| Mist (light default) | *(none)* |
| Slate (dark default) | `dark` |
| Bright | `theme-bright` |
| Dark-deep | `dark theme-deep` |
| Tenant brand (future) | `theme-<tenant>` (+ `dark` if dark base) |

Full token values: `globals.css`. Visual proof of all modes: the style tile + the OwedBook Mist/Slate/Dark artifacts in `_design/`.

---

# THEME LIBRARY — the factory theme catalog

> **Version:** 1.2 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active
> **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK, TOKEN_FILE, THEMING_MANUAL, DESIGNER_PLAYBOOK

> **Scope:** first family — **Metro Warm** (Cyber Pharma: Mist / Slate / Bright / Dark-deep). Further theme families append here as new projects derive them; the pattern is app-agnostic.
> **Reader:** Designer (me, in future labs) + Claudy.
> **Pairs with:** the **Global Design System Handbook** (defines the token *contract*) and each project's **token file** (`globals.css` — the live values). This doc is the *catalog*: named themes that each satisfy the contract.
> **Mental model:** the Handbook says *which tokens must exist*; `globals.css` holds *the active values*; this library is the *menu* of complete value-sets you can drop in. Adding a theme never touches the contract — only values.
>
> **v1.1 reconciliation note (2026-06-08):** Two changes only. (1) The live token file is **`globals.css`**, not `TOKEN_FILE.md` — references corrected throughout (the Global Design System Handbook §8 names `globals.css` as the primary deliverable; this aligns to it). (2) Role identity tokens (`--role-*`): the RULES were written here (§2). *(v1.2 note: they are now **defined in the contract** — GDSH §2 — with **reference values minted in TOKEN_FILE**; the reconciliation this note started is complete on both sides, F-043.)*

---

## 1. How a theme entry works

A theme = **one complete semantic token set** (every token the Handbook requires), in HSL-no-wrapper, activated by a class on `<html>`. Components never change; only the variables behind `bg-primary`, `bg-card`, etc. resolve differently. That's the whole "change values, not code" promise.

- **Light-base themes** live on `:root` (or a `.theme-*` override).
- **Dark-base themes** live on `.dark` (or `.dark.theme-*`).
- Full values for the two defaults are in `globals.css` (`:root` + `.dark`); the alternates are the small `.theme-*` override blocks there.

---

## 2. The "Metro Warm" family (Cyber Pharma v1)

Shared across **all four** (these never change between modes — brand + meaning + identity hold):

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary (brand) | coral `#f9704f` → `12 93% 64%` |
| Success (recovered) | green — `131 54% 40%` light / `142 69% 58%` dark |
| Destructive (money lost) | red — `2 67% 51%` light / `351 95% 71%` dark |
| Info (neutral count) | blue `#2f7ce0` → `214 74% 53%` |
| Warning (pending) | amber `#e8a008` → `41 93% 47%` |
| Role — superadmin | identity hue, distinct from brand & status *(set per family; AA on `--card`)* |
| Role — admin | identity hue — **must not reuse the destructive red** |
| Role — member | identity hue — may align with `--success` |
| Typeface | Saira |
| Radius | `0` (Metro flat) |
| Labels | uppercase, tracked |

> **Role tokens (added v1.1):** roles are identities, not statuses. They hold their hue across all four modes just like the semantic four. The only hard rule: `--role-admin` must read as visually distinct from `--destructive` so an admin badge never looks like an error. Tune each role's lightness per mode and contrast-check on the style tile.

What changes between modes is **only the neutral surface stack**:

### 🟫 Mist — *default light*
- **Base:** light · **Background:** `#e2e5ea` (`217 16% 90%`) · **Surface:** `#ffffff`
- **Activate:** `:root` (default — no class)
- **Best for:** the everyday daytime view. Muted, easy on the eyes, looks intentional rather than glaring. **This is the recommended default.**

### 🌑 Slate — *default dark*
- **Base:** dark · **Background:** `#1d212a` (`222 18% 14%`) · **Surface (card):** `#2e3440` (`220 16% 22%`)
- **Activate:** `class="dark"`
- **Best for:** low-light work, long sessions. Sophisticated gunmetal; coral pops hardest here.
- **Readability note (L16):** background sits *below* the card so panels elevate; `--muted-foreground` is lifted (`221 17% 71%`) and `--border` firmed (`218 13% 33%`). This is the v1.1 real-screen fix — keep it; do not flatten background and card to the same value.

### ⬜ Bright — *alternate light*
- **Base:** light · **Background:** `#ffffff` · **Surface:** `#ffffff`
- **Activate:** `class="theme-bright"`
- **Best for:** maximum contrast, print/export views, screenshots for decks. Crisp but can glare on big screens.

### ⬛ Dark-deep — *alternate dark*
- **Base:** dark · **Background:** `#191c24` (`224 18% 12%`) · **Surface:** `#23262f`
- **Activate:** `class="dark theme-deep"`
- **Best for:** OLED / focus mode / demo drama. Near-black; reserve for when you want the charts to glow.

**Phase 1 ships Mist + Slate** wired to the theme toggle. Bright and Dark-deep are catalogued and ready, not yet wired.

---

## 3. Adding a new theme (the repeatable process)

1. **Pick the neutral direction** — only the surface stack changes (background, card, muted, border, secondary). Brand + semantic + role stay fixed.
2. **Derive the full set** — every token the Handbook lists, light *and*/or dark base. Don't ship a partial theme.
3. **Contrast-check** — run `success`/`destructive` (and the `--role-*` colors) as small text against the new `card`; tune lightness until all clear WCAG AA. (This is the step a 4-color palette can't give you.)
4. **Add as a class** — a `.theme-*` override block in `globals.css`. Nothing else changes.
5. **Catalog it here** — name, base, background, "best for", activation class.
6. **Render the style tile in it** — eyeball light + dark, then a real-screen pass, before locking.

A new theme is ~30 minutes and zero component changes. That's the payoff.

---

## 4. Per-tenant brand themes (multi-tenant, future)

Cyber Pharma is multi-tenant. When a client wants their own brand color, it's the same mechanism scoped to a class:

```css
.theme-acme { --primary: <acme hsl>; --ring: <acme hsl>; --accent: <acme hsl>; }
```

- Swap **only** `--primary` / `--accent` / `--ring`. **Never** the semantic four or the role tokens — underpaid must read red, and an admin must read like an admin, for every client.
- Apply the class at the tenant boundary (layout reads the org's theme).
- This keeps a per-pharmacy brand a one-line addition, not a fork.

> Defer building this until multi-tenant brand theming is actually scoped (it's Phase 7-ish). The architecture above means it costs nothing to add later.

---

## 5. Quick reference — activation

| Theme | Class on `<html>` |
|---|---|
| Mist (light default) | *(none)* |
| Slate (dark default) | `dark` |
| Bright | `theme-bright` |
| Dark-deep | `dark theme-deep` |
| Tenant brand (future) | `theme-<tenant>` (+ `dark` if dark base) |

Full token values: `globals.css`. Visual proof of all modes: the style tile + the OwedBook Mist/Slate/Dark artifacts in `_design/`.

# UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No horizontal scroll** at any width below desktop - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. Resist token sprawl. ### What Violates Rule Zero-B These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Hardcoded hex codes in component files** (e.g., `bg-[#3b82f6]`, `style={{ color: "#000" }}`) 2. **Tailwind color names that bypass tokens** (e.g., `bg-blue-500` instead of `bg-primary`) 3. **Light mode only** — tokens declared in `:root` with no `.dark` override set 4. **Designer delivers only a Figma file** — no executable tokens file provided 5. **Component overrides the palette silently** — fabricator bypasses a token "because it didn't fit" instead of surfacing the token as wrong ### How To Honor Rule Zero-B In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout: 1. **Identify which semantic tokens this component needs** (e.g., a button needs `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`) 2. **Use the token via the Tailwind utility class** (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) 3. **Never reach for a literal color value** — if the design calls for a color outside the current tokens, surface to the operator before bypassing the system ### Cross-Reference - **`THEMING_MANUAL.md`** — the deep dive on token architecture, designer deliverable format, and quick-swap workflow - **`APP_ARCHITECTURE_MANUAL.md`** §Theming Files — where the token files live in the repo - **`HANDOFF_PACKAGE_PLAYBOOK.md`** §Designer Handoff — the designer engagement spec - **Cyberize Run 001 `_project/CLAUDE.md`** — the canonical worked example of a Locked Palette table ### Why Rule Zero-B Supersedes Other Color Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc specifies a literal color value instead of a token reference, the conflict resolves in favor of Rule Zero-B. **Tokens are the contract.** Surface the conflict to the operator and update the other doc. > **Note on §10.5 (Dark Mode Best Practices) and §10.8 (Do's and Don'ts):** Those sections already endorse semantic tokens and forbid hardcoded hex. # UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No horizontal scroll** at any width below desktop - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. Resist token sprawl. ### What Violates Rule Zero-B These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Hardcoded hex codes in component files** (e.g., `bg-[#3b82f6]`, `style={{ color: "#000" }}`) 2. **Tailwind color names that bypass tokens** (e.g., `bg-blue-500` instead of `bg-primary`) 3. **Light mode only** — tokens declared in `:root` with no `.dark` override set 4. **Designer delivers only a Figma file** — no executable tokens file provided 5. **Component overrides the palette silently** — fabricator bypasses a token "because it didn't fit" instead of surfacing the token as wrong ### How To Honor Rule Zero-B In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout: 1. **Identify which semantic tokens this component needs** (e.g., a button needs `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`) 2. **Use the token via the Tailwind utility class** (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) 3. **Never reach for a literal color value** — if the design calls for a color outside the current tokens, surface to the operator before bypassing the system ### Cross-Reference - **`THEMING_MANUAL.md`** — the deep dive on token architecture, designer deliverable format, and quick-swap workflow - **`APP_ARCHITECTURE_MANUAL.md`** §Theming Files — where the token files live in the repo - **`HANDOFF_PACKAGE_PLAYBOOK.md`** §Designer Handoff — the designer engagement spec - **Cyberize Run 001 `_project/CLAUDE.md`** — the canonical worked example of a Locked Palette table ### Why Rule Zero-B Supersedes Other Color Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc specifies a literal color value instead of a token reference, the conflict resolves in favor of Rule Zero-B. **Tokens are the contract.** Surface the conflict to the operator and update the other doc. > **Note on §10.5 (Dark Mode Best Practices) and §10.8 (Do's and Don'ts):** Those sections already endorse semantic tokens and forbid hardcoded hex. Rule Zero-B promotes that guidance to foundational-posture status and makes it enforceable at every phase gate, not just a best practice. --- ## Philosophy & Approach This manual documents the **proven patterns** used in this starter kit. The goal is to build apps **faster and better** by: 1. **Separating concerns** - Keep `page.tsx` minimal, content in dedicated files 2. **Reusing components** - Use common layout components for consistency 3. **Mobile-first responsive** - Every layout must work on all screen sizes 4. **Consistent naming** - Follow strict file and component naming conventions 5. **Composition over complexity** - Build with simple, composable pieces **Core Principle:** If vibe coders can ship fast without deep knowledge, we as engineers should ship **faster and better** with our structured approach. --- ## Table of Contents 0. # UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No horizontal scroll** at any width below desktop - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. Resist token sprawl. ### What Violates Rule Zero-B These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Hardcoded hex codes in component files** (e.g., `bg-[#3b82f6]`, `style={{ color: "#000" }}`) 2. **Tailwind color names that bypass tokens** (e.g., `bg-blue-500` instead of `bg-primary`) 3. **Light mode only** — tokens declared in `:root` with no `.dark` override set 4. **Designer delivers only a Figma file** — no executable tokens file provided 5. **Component overrides the palette silently** — fabricator bypasses a token "because it didn't fit" instead of surfacing the token as wrong ### How To Honor Rule Zero-B In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout: 1. **Identify which semantic tokens this component needs** (e.g., a button needs `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`) 2. **Use the token via the Tailwind utility class** (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) 3. **Never reach for a literal color value** — if the design calls for a color outside the current tokens, surface to the operator before bypassing the system ### Cross-Reference - **`THEMING_MANUAL.md`** — the deep dive on token architecture, designer deliverable format, and quick-swap workflow - **`APP_ARCHITECTURE_MANUAL.md`** §Theming Files — where the token files live in the repo - **`HANDOFF_PACKAGE_PLAYBOOK.md`** §Designer Handoff — the designer engagement spec - **Cyberize Run 001 `_project/CLAUDE.md`** — the canonical worked example of a Locked Palette table ### Why Rule Zero-B Supersedes Other Color Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc specifies a literal color value instead of a token reference, the conflict resolves in favor of Rule Zero-B. **Tokens are the contract.** Surface the conflict to the operator and update the other doc. > **Note on §10.5 (Dark Mode Best Practices) and §10.8 (Do's and Don'ts):** Those sections already endorse semantic tokens and forbid hardcoded hex. # UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No horizontal scroll** at any width below desktop - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. Resist token sprawl. ### What Violates Rule Zero-B These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Hardcoded hex codes in component files** (e.g., `bg-[#3b82f6]`, `style={{ color: "#000" }}`) 2. **Tailwind color names that bypass tokens** (e.g., `bg-blue-500` instead of `bg-primary`) 3. **Light mode only** — tokens declared in `:root` with no `.dark` override set 4. **Designer delivers only a Figma file** — no executable tokens file provided 5. **Component overrides the palette silently** — fabricator bypasses a token "because it didn't fit" instead of surfacing the token as wrong ### How To Honor Rule Zero-B In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout: 1. **Identify which semantic tokens this component needs** (e.g., a button needs `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`) 2. **Use the token via the Tailwind utility class** (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) 3. **Never reach for a literal color value** — if the design calls for a color outside the current tokens, surface to the operator before bypassing the system ### Cross-Reference - **`THEMING_MANUAL.md`** — the deep dive on token architecture, designer deliverable format, and quick-swap workflow - **`APP_ARCHITECTURE_MANUAL.md`** §Theming Files — where the token files live in the repo - **`HANDOFF_PACKAGE_PLAYBOOK.md`** §Designer Handoff — the designer engagement spec - **Cyberize Run 001 `_project/CLAUDE.md`** — the canonical worked example of a Locked Palette table ### Why Rule Zero-B Supersedes Other Color Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc specifies a literal color value instead of a token reference, the conflict resolves in favor of Rule Zero-B. **Tokens are the contract.** Surface the conflict to the operator and update the other doc. > **Note on §10.5 (Dark Mode Best Practices) and §10.8 (Do's and Don'ts):** Those sections already endorse semantic tokens and forbid hardcoded hex. Rule Zero-B promotes that guidance to foundational-posture status and makes it enforceable at every phase gate, not just a best practice. --- ## Philosophy & Approach This manual documents the **proven patterns** used in this starter kit. ## 9. Phase 7: Authentication & RBAC

For kit-based builds, consume the existing kit authentication and authorization primitives and verify them through AUTH-WALK. Do not rebuild login pages, an auth store, metadata role flags or a client route guard. Page wrappers follow STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK §5 and §7: resolve authorized server data before rendering the interactive client child. Generic non-kit examples do not apply when the kit supplies the capability.

The role table is the only authorization authority. Never authorize from user_metadata or a profile mirror. Superadmin creation is console-only; no app-side superadmin creation route is provided. Retire the metadata-authorized add-user, delete-user and get-users recipes. Future privileged list/delete operations remain possible only with trusted current-role lookup, operation-local authorization before elevated capability, an approved target-role allowlist and privileged-target protection. Profile mirrors contain profile data, not authorization columns. Registration metadata is not authorization.

Every privileged operation authorizes its own invocation before acquiring or using elevated capability: authenticate the requester, resolve the current trusted role, authorize the operation and target, and validate input. Layout admission controls page access only. Direct unauthenticated, wrong-role and wrong-target invocations must produce no privileged side effect.

Verify authentication state, table-backed current role, object-level authorization, denied targets, session expiry, logout and first server render. The former metadata-role/auth-store checklist is withdrawn. Kit-dependent signatures require the pinned kit evidence; this containment does not close those replacements.

# UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No unintended page-level horizontal overflow** below desktop; bounded intentional tabs/carousels are permitted with accessible controls. - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. Resist token sprawl. ### What Violates Rule Zero-B These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Hardcoded hex codes in component files** (e.g., `bg-[#3b82f6]`, `style={{ color: "#000" }}`) 2. **Tailwind color names that bypass tokens** (e.g., `bg-blue-500` instead of `bg-primary`) 3. **Light mode only** — tokens declared in `:root` with no `.dark` override set 4. **Designer delivers only a Figma file** — no executable tokens file provided 5. **Component overrides the palette silently** — fabricator bypasses a token "because it didn't fit" instead of surfacing the token as wrong ### How To Honor Rule Zero-B In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout: 1. **Identify which semantic tokens this component needs** (e.g., a button needs `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`) 2. **Use the token via the Tailwind utility class** (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) 3. **Never reach for a literal color value** — if the design calls for a color outside the current tokens, surface to the operator before bypassing the system ### Cross-Reference - **`THEMING_MANUAL.md`** — the deep dive on token architecture, designer deliverable format, and quick-swap workflow - **`TOKEN_FILE.md`** §1 Entry stylesheet — where the token files live in the repo - **`GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK.md`** §8 The Designer’s deliverables — the designer engagement spec - **Cyberize Run 001 `_project/CLAUDE.md`** — the canonical worked example of a Locked Palette table ### Why Rule Zero-B Supersedes Other Color Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc specifies a literal color value instead of a token reference, the conflict resolves in favor of Rule Zero-B. **Tokens are the contract.** Surface the conflict to the operator and update the other doc. > **Note on §10.5 (Dark Mode Best Practices) and §10.8 (Do's and Don'ts):** Those sections already endorse semantic tokens and forbid hardcoded hex. # UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No unintended page-level horizontal overflow** below desktop; bounded intentional tabs/carousels are permitted with accessible controls. - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. # UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No unintended page-level horizontal overflow** below desktop; bounded intentional tabs/carousels are permitted with accessible controls. - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. Resist token sprawl. ### What Violates Rule Zero-B These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Hardcoded hex codes in component files** (e.g., `bg-[#3b82f6]`, `style={{ color: "#000" }}`) 2. **Tailwind color names that bypass tokens** (e.g., `bg-blue-500` instead of `bg-primary`) 3. **Light mode only** — tokens declared in `:root` with no `.dark` override set 4. **Designer delivers only a Figma file** — no executable tokens file provided 5. **Component overrides the palette silently** — fabricator bypasses a token "because it didn't fit" instead of surfacing the token as wrong ### How To Honor Rule Zero-B In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout: 1. **Identify which semantic tokens this component needs** (e.g., a button needs `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`) 2. **Use the token via the Tailwind utility class** (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) 3. **Never reach for a literal color value** — if the design calls for a color outside the current tokens, surface to the operator before bypassing the system ### Cross-Reference - **`THEMING_MANUAL.md`** — the deep dive on token architecture, designer deliverable format, and quick-swap workflow - **`TOKEN_FILE.md`** §1 Entry stylesheet — where the token files live in the repo - **`GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK.md`** §8 The Designer’s deliverables — the designer engagement spec - **Cyberize Run 001 `_project/CLAUDE.md`** — the canonical worked example of a Locked Palette table ### Why Rule Zero-B Supersedes Other Color Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc specifies a literal color value instead of a token reference, the conflict resolves in favor of Rule Zero-B. **Tokens are the contract.** Surface the conflict to the operator and update the other doc. > **Note on §10.5 (Dark Mode Best Practices) and §10.8 (Do's and Don'ts):** Those sections already endorse semantic tokens and forbid hardcoded hex. # UI/UX BUILDING MANUAL > **Version:** 1.4 · **Date:** 2026-07-08 · **Status:** Active > **Tier:** 5 — Design System · **Pairs with:** STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK, COMPONENT_REGISTRY, THEMING_MANUAL, FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK, GLOBAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM_HANDBOOK > **Project:** Stark SaaS Starter Kit > **Purpose:** Standardized guide for building pages and components consistently across all projects --- ## ⚡ RULE ZERO — MOBILE-FIRST IS THE FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **If you read no other section of this manual, read this one.** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries is mobile-first. > This is not a feature, not a verification step, not a polish pass. > It is the operating posture that the entire manual rests on. ### The Operating Posture - **Design starts at 375 pixels.** The mobile experience is the canonical version of the UI. Desktop is progressive enhancement on top of mobile, never the other way around. - **Scale UP from mobile.** Breakpoints add desktop affordances. They never strip mobile features. - **Layouts that work at desktop but break at mobile are FAILURES**, not "polish needed." They are F-grade work by the operator's standard. - **Mobile responsiveness is a foundation, not a verification gate.** The mobile sketch comes before the desktop sketch. The mobile breakpoint behavior is in the file's opening JSDoc BEFORE the component is written. ### Required Breakpoints (Non-Negotiable) | Breakpoint | Width | Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Mobile** | 375px | Default; everything works here first | | **Tablet** | 768px (`md:`) | Layouts may split. Narrow nav rails may persist; **wide app rails (≥ ~20rem) stay a slide-over** (they don't fit yet) | | **Desktop** | 1024px+ (`lg:`) | Full multi-column layouts permitted; wide app rails become persistent here | Every UI screen MUST be verified at all three breakpoints before phase completion. ### The Grading Rule > *Any UI/UX design gets an F if it's not mobile responsive.* — Stark This is not a suggestion. This is the operating standard. It applies at every gate, in every phase, on every component. ### Implementation Discipline - **Touch targets:** 44 pixels minimum on any interactive element - **Sidebars:** Slide-over below the breakpoint where the rail actually fits — `lg` (1024) for wide app rails (≥ ~20rem), `md` (768) for narrow nav. Never persistent at a width the rail can't fit, and never *absent* below it: a hamburger/trigger to open the slide-over is mandatory. A fixed sidebar with `hidden md:block` and no trigger = the rail vanishes on mobile = automatic failure. - **Type sizes:** Readable at 375px without zoom (no smaller than 14px body text) - **Spacing:** Tap-friendly padding, not pixel-economy - **No unintended page-level horizontal overflow** below desktop; bounded intentional tabs/carousels are permitted with accessible controls. - **All controls reachable** at mobile (no "desktop only" UI hidden at mobile) ### What Violates Rule Zero These are AUTOMATIC FAILURES at any phase gate: 1. **Fixed-width sidebars** (`w-64`, `w-72`) without responsive collapse to hamburger/slide-over 2. **Layouts that overflow horizontally** at 375px 3. **Touch targets smaller than 44px** on any interactive element 4. **Text or controls hidden at mobile** but available at desktop 5. **"We'll fix mobile later"** attitude — this is the deferred-violation pattern. Catch the first time, surface immediately, refuse to advance. 6. **No mobile sketch in the plan** — if the plan doesn't describe the 375px layout, the file is not authored ### How To Honor Rule Zero In Authoring Before authoring any UI component, page, or layout, answer in the file's opening JSDoc: 1. **What's the 375px sketch?** (1-3 sentences describing the mobile layout) 2. **What changes at 768px?** (the tablet/md breakpoint behavior) 3. **What changes at 1024px?** (the desktop/lg breakpoint behavior) 4. **Are all touch targets ≥ 44px?** (yes/no with note if exceptions exist) If you cannot answer all four, STOP — surface to the operator. The file is not authored until the mobile-first contract is explicit. ### Cross-Reference - **`STARTER_KIT_HANDBOOK.md`** — kit primitives that are already mobile-first (AppShellPage, Sheet, etc.) - **`COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md`** — per-primitive mobile behavior reference - **`FRONTEND_BUILD_PHASE_PLAYBOOK.md`** — phase preambles that re-inject mobile-first at execution moments ### Why Rule Zero Supersedes Other Doctrine If another section of this manual or another factory doc conflicts with Rule Zero, surface the conflict immediately — **Rule Zero wins**. Mobile-first is foundational, not negotiable. All other patterns and conventions in this manual are layered on top of the mobile-first foundation. --- ## 🎨 RULE ZERO-B — THEMING IS THE SECOND FOUNDATIONAL POSTURE > **Companion to Rule Zero (mobile-first). If Rule Zero says "design for 375 pixels first," Rule Zero-B says "design tokens before pixels."** > Every UI/UX deliverable from Stark Industries reads colors from semantic tokens, never from hardcoded values. > This posture exists so brand iteration is a five-minute operation, not an hour-long refactor. ### The Operating Posture - **Every color in every component reads from a semantic token.** Tokens are CSS custom properties declared in `src/app/globals.css` and mapped through `tailwind.config.ts`. - **No hardcoded hex codes in component files.** Not in inline styles. Not in Tailwind utility classes that bypass tokens. Not in CSS files outside `globals.css`. - **Light mode AND dark mode tokens declared from Phase 1.** Both sets coexist in the same file; the browser picks which renders. - **The designer's executable deliverable is the tokens file, not a Figma export.** Figma is for human communication; tokens are for fabrication. ### Required Semantic Tokens (Minimum) Every Stark project declares these tokens (matching shadcn convention so the kit ecosystem works out of the box): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` Additional tokens (`--success`, `--warning`) may be added when a real project need surfaces. ## 6. Cart Logic

**Executable example withdrawn.** The previous example is not an approved implementation. The outgoing archived document preserves it as history. Replacement code requires the project’s approved contract, verified dependency interfaces and behavioral evidence. This withdrawal contains the misleading recipe; it does not certify the underlying finding resolved.

Keep hydration readiness outside the resettable business state. A normal reset preserves readiness. Hydration finishes in ready or error; an error exposes bounded recovery and never leaves an indefinite loading state. Verify reset after hydration, invalid stored data and unavailable storage.

The browser may display or poll payment status; it may not choose paid or processing state. A payment-derived transition requires verified server-side evidence bound to the stored order and payment attempt, including amount and currency. Non-webhook mutations authenticate and authorize the operation and target, including an explicitly approved guest capability where supported, then validate the state transition.

## 4. The Module Package (one folder, self-contained)

```

├── CLAUDE.md                    ← THE MANAGER — always read first (see §5)
├── MODULE_BRIEF.md              ← scope lock, gates, forbidden zones (larger modules)
├── DATA_CONTRACT_AMENDMENT.md   ← only when wire contracts change
